lesson.title: Understand lodging law and records accurately
lesson.reading: りょかんぎょうほうときろくをただしくりかいする

objectives.text: Explain the relationship between permission, facility standards and hygiene
Distinguish the three business categories without relying on price
Check current guest-register fields and the retention period

sections.title: Permission and facility standards
sections.body: The Hotel Business Act concerns proper operation of accommodation businesses and public health. Operating a lodging business generally requires permission from the prefectural governor or equivalent authority. In cities with public health centers and in special wards, the authority is the mayor or ward mayor. Distinguish the consultation office from the legal permission-granting authority. Check structural and equipment standards for room size, ventilation, natural light, toilets and washbasins. Operators and managers confirm applicable standards with the public health center or other authority according to business category, local ordinances and equipment conditions; frontline staff report abnormalities or changes.

sections.title: Use definitions to distinguish the three categories
sections.body: The Act distinguishes hotel/ryokan business, simple lodging business and boarding-house business. Simple lodging primarily provides structures and equipment for shared sleeping accommodation by many people; it does not simply mean inexpensive accommodation. Boarding-house business charges accommodation fees by units of at least one month. A single long-stay guest does not by itself determine the category. Check the permitted business category and statutory definition rather than deciding from the name or price.

sections.title: Check current register fields and retention
sections.body: Prepare accurate guest registers and store them appropriately. Under the implementing regulations checked on October 31, 2026, record names, addresses, contact details and other required information, and retain the register for three years from its creation. Additional nationality and passport-number fields apply to foreign guests who do not have an address in Japan. Check any additional local requirements. Do not teach the textbook’s occupation field as a current basic requirement under this Act. Standardize the collection purpose, required fields, storage location and authorized access within the facility, and prevent personal-data leaks.

sections.title: Use records to verify hygiene and safety measures
sections.body: Maintain cleaning, disinfection and pest control, and properly manage fire-safety equipment and escape routes. Safety measures may arise not only from lodging law but also fire-safety legislation and local ordinances. Following an inspection or direction from a public health center or local authority, organize the findings, responsible staff, deadlines and improvement results and confirm corrective action. Depending on the violation, suspension, cancellation of permission or penalties may apply. Do not conceal problems from the person in charge or guess penalty amounts when explaining them.

example.situation: A new employee says registers require occupation and inexpensive accommodation is called simple lodging.
steps: Check current register fields and correct the distinction between occupation and contact details.
Confirm the business category by the statutory structure-and-equipment definition, not price.
Notify the staff responsible for updating explanations and forms.

practice.prompt: For permission, categories, registers and supervision, write one point requiring a current-system check rather than relying only on the textbook.
expectedPoints: Distinguish the consultation office from the permission authority
Simple lodging is not a low-price category

questions.prompt: Which understanding of simple lodging is appropriate?
choices: The lowest-priced accommodation always qualifies
Focus on structures and equipment primarily for shared sleeping accommodation by many people
Any long-stay guest makes it qualify
The name hotel rules it out
questions.explanation: Check statutory definitions and permission, not just price or name.

questions.prompt: Which are current basic guest-register fields under lodging law?
choices: Name, address and occupation only
Name only
Name, address, contact details and other required information
The guest’s salary
questions.explanation: Contact details have replaced occupation as a basic field. Confirm the scope of additional foreign-guest information according to residence in Japan and other conditions.

questions.prompt: How should guest registers be retained?
choices: For three years from creation
Discard immediately after check-out
According to the staff member’s preference
Only until the next morning
questions.explanation: Follow the retention period in the implementing regulations while also protecting personal information.

questions.prompt: What should a manager do after public health center directions?
choices: No record is needed because the directions were oral
Keep it secret within one department
Wait until a problem occurs
Record findings, responsible staff, deadlines and improvement results, and confirm correction
questions.explanation: Record responsibility and results so improvements can be carried out and verified.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate regarding business permission and facility standards?
choices: Assume inexpensive lodging needs no permission
Every consultation officer is the legal permission authority
Check the permission authority and business category and verify room size, ventilation, natural light and sanitary-equipment standards
Decide the business category from one room name
questions.explanation: Distinguish location and business conditions, and do not confuse consultation with the legal permission authority.

questions.prompt: Which criterion describes boarding-house business in the lesson?
choices: Any single long-stay guest makes every business a boarding house
Low prices always mean boarding-house business
Two beds in a room mean boarding-house business
Charging accommodation fees in units of one month or longer
questions.explanation: Check the permitted category and statutory definition, rather than only one guest’s stay duration.

questions.prompt: What is the basic role of the Hotel Business Act?
choices: Determining only guest preferences
Concerning proper operation of accommodation businesses and public health
Eliminating all fire-safety legislation
Determining only room discount rates
questions.explanation: It relates to operations, structure and equipment, hygiene and required records. Check other laws and ordinances too.

questions.prompt: What should managers understand about violations or deficiencies?
choices: Guessing a penalty amount resolves a violation
Keep no report even after guidance
Depending on the issue, suspension or cancellation of permission may follow, so report and verify correction
Hide problems if outsiders cannot see them
questions.explanation: Correct issues according to law and official guidance; do not guess penalty amounts.

questions.prompt: What is appropriate daily hygiene management in lodging facilities?
choices: Continue regular cleaning, disinfection and pest control and report abnormalities
Clean only on inspection days
Do not clean places guests cannot see
Only record that disinfection occurred without doing it
questions.explanation: Hygiene management is ongoing, not only work after inspection. Follow facility procedures and report abnormalities for action.

questions.prompt: After studying hygiene under lodging law, a worker checks fire equipment and escape routes. What is appropriate?
choices: Reading lodging law removes the need to check fire standards
Equipment needs no checks after installation
Unknown escape routes need no report because they are separate from hygiene
Manage equipment and routes and confirm applicable fire legislation and local ordinances with responsible staff
questions.explanation: Do not limit the basis of safety measures to lodging law. Manage equipment and routes and check relevant standards and procedures.

questions.prompt: Which set gives the statutory business categories in the lesson?
choices: Single, twin and suite
Hotel/ryokan business, simple lodging business and boarding-house business
Breakfast included, two meals included and room only
Front desk, cooking and cleaning
questions.explanation: Business categories differ from room types, packages and departments. Check each statutory definition as well as names.

questions.prompt: Which approach to guest-register creation and storage follows the lesson?
choices: Asking only a name removes the need for records or storage
Anyone may freely take guest information home
Confirm required fields and retention conditions under current applicable rules, prepare accurately and store appropriately
Invent a retention period not given in the material
questions.explanation: Check register fields and retention separately. Creating a record does not end the storage obligation; also check information protection and applicable rules.
